title: Double Caching (Application Cache over OS Page Cache)
pattern: An application manually loading and caching entire raw files in heap-allocated strings or memory blocks to "avoid disk reading latency."
why_bad: Modern operating systems automatically cache files in the physical RAM page cache (buffer cache). Re-implementing this cache in application memory wastes physical RAM, triggers double memory copies, and bypasses OS-level page eviction algorithms (like LRU) [118, 140, 164].
detection: A custom in-memory global vector or map holding the exact contents of static database files or text files on disk that are read repetitively.
counterexample: Compilers or static site generators that read and compile source code to an AST in-memory structure once. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Read the files directly using standard buffered I/O stream functions (`std::io::BufReader`) and let the OS page cache handle RAM caching.
